st: Bring [[5 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Lower the heat to medium. Pour in [[1.5 cups]] cornmeal in a thin stream, whisking constantly to stop lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon. Cook on low, stirring often, for 25 minutes until very thick and pulling from the sides.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] butter.
Turn the mămăligă onto a board or plate and shape into a mound. Traditionally cut it into slices with a string.
Serve hot topped with [[1 cup]] crumbled cheese and [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.

ing: large, cored, or 1 jar pickled cabbage leaves
st: Boil the whole cabbage head in salted water 10 minutes, then peel off the soft leaves. Trim thick ribs. Shred the leftover cabbage and spread half in a pot.
Cook the chopped onions in [[3 tbsp]] oil for 6 minutes until soft. Cool slightly.
Mix the onions with the pork, rice, dill, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Put a heaped spoon of filling at the base of each leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Pack the rolls seam side down in the pot over the shredded cabbage. Add the bay leaves.
Mix the grated tomatoes, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[2 cups]] water and pour over the rolls. Cover with a plate to hold them down.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low for 2 hours until the cabbage is soft and pork reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with [[1 cup]] sour cream and mămăligă if you like.

ing: divided: 3 for dough, 3 for the pan
or crumbled feta mixed with ricotta
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[0.75 cup]] warm water, [[3 tbsp]] oil and [[1 tsp]] vinegar and knead 8 minutes until soft and elastic.
Cover the dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix [[1.5 cups]] cheese, the egg, dill and [[0.25 tsp]] salt for the filling.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each into a thin circle about 7 inches wide.
Put filling on half of the circle, fold over, and press and crimp the edges to seal.
Heat a skillet with [[3 tbsp]] oil over medium heat. Cook the pastries 3 to 4 minutes per side until blistered and golden.
Brush with [[3 tbsp]] melted butter and serve warm.

ing: whole cut up, or bone-in pieces
fermented wheat bran liquid or fresh lemon juice
st: Put the chicken, [[10 cups]] water, the whole onion and [[2 tsp]] salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Simmer gently for 40 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and is tender.
Lift out the chicken and onion. Shred the meat, discarding skin and bones, and dice the onion.
Add the carrots, celery and bell pepper to the broth. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add [[5 oz]] noodles and cook 6 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken and onion to the pot. Stir in [[0.25 cup]] lovage or celery leaves and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Stir in [[0.33 cup]] borș or lemon juice until pleasantly sour. Add dill and serve hot.
Put the beef and pork in a large bowl. Add [[6 cloves]] minced garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] baking soda, [[1 tsp]] thyme, [[1 tsp]] paprika, [[0.5 tsp]] coriander, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] cold broth a little at a time while mixing with your hands for 5 minutes until sticky.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour so the flavors settle.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into fat sausages about 3 inches long and 1 inch wide.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and the center reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with mustard and bread.
Soak the pork in cold water 1 hour, then rinse. Put it in a large pot and cover with cold water, bring to a boil and boil for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Return the pork to the pot with [[10 cups]] fresh water, the onion, carrots, [[6 cloves]] garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, skim off foam, then simmer on very low heat for 4 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Strain the broth. Pull the meat from the bones and shred it. Slice the carrots.
Crush [[2 cloves]] garlic and stir into the warm broth with the dill.
Arrange the meat and carrots in a dish and pour the broth over to cover.
Chill at least 6 hours until set. Serve cold in slices with horseradish.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, 2 eggs, [[1 tsp]] salt and about [[0.5 cup]] warm water into a firm dough. Knead 8 minutes, cover, and rest 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 minutes until soft. Drain and mash.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter and cook the onion 6 minutes. Mix into the potatoes with the cheese, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 3 inch rounds. Put a small spoon of filling in each.
Fold over and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Boil in salted water in batches for 5 minutes after they float.
Toss in [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and serve with [[1 cup]] sour cream.

ing: medium, tops cut and seeds removed
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion and carrot 6 minutes until soft. Cool.
Mix the vegetables with the pork, rice, dill, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Fill each pepper about three-quarters full. Cover with the cut tops.
Stand the peppers upright in a snug pot.
Mix the grated tomatoes, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] water and pour around the peppers.
Cover and simmer gently 1 hour 10 minutes until the peppers are soft and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with sauce and [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[1 cup]] warm milk, [[6 tbsp]] melted butter, 1 egg and lemon zest.
Knead 10 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and let rise 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Beat the cottage cheese with 2 eggs, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] vanilla and [[0.5 cup]] raisins for the filling.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll two thirds of the dough to line a greased 9-inch springform pan, going up the sides.
Pour the sweet cheese filling into the dough-lined pan and level the top.
Roll the rest of the dough into strips and form a lattice over the top, pressing the ends into the sides.
Rest 20 minutes, then bake 45 minutes until golden and the filling is set.
Cool fully in the pan before slicing.
